Frustration is the blocking of behavior that will help to reach a goal.� This means that people want to follow a certain course of action but their efforts are not working.��

For example, you may have wanted to go into a certain career, but you have found that you don t have the proper skills or finances to pursue that career.�

Some frustrations are short lived, while others may be much more long-term.

Frustration blocking is the ability to handle frustration without becoming too upset. People act in different ways when facing frustrations.� They may withdraw or become angry. Well-adjusted people may accept some frustration as normal, and rather than feeling hopeless, they may readjust their goals and plan around the frustrations.
